requirements.title: The /graph page footer shall display the application name and current semantic version matching the value declared in package.json

vision.section: CLAUDE.md — Tool Hygiene & Operability: Version exposure
vision.paraphrase: Baseline tool-hygiene requirement: CLAUDE.md declares the web app's version-exposure mechanism is a footer display, since there is no server runtime for a /version endpoint.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall display a user-facing error message naming the problem and the next user action when graph-data.json or vector-index.json fails to load

vision.paraphrase: The Next.js page must gracefully handle failures when fetching static graph and vector assets with helpful user-facing error messaging.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall fetch graph-data.json and vector-index.json client-side on load and render all nodes and edges via react-force-graph without requiring any backend call after page load

vision.paraphrase: Live-feeling static graph achieved by fetching precomputed graph-data.json client-side and rendering with react-force-graph.
The Next.js page fetches static graph-data.json and vector-index.json assets client-side and renders via react-force-graph with no backend calls.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor lands on /graph, the page fetches graph-data.json and vector-index.json from static assets.
The dev server locally runs the Next.js page, which fetches the locally-built graph-data.json and vector-index.json.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall render each edge from graph-data.json as a visible connecting line between the corresponding node pair

vision.paraphrase: Force-directed graph layout renders all edges from graph-data.json as visible connecting lines.

conops.paraphrase: The force-directed graph renders connecting lines for all edges, making relationships visible.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall color each node according to its folder/taxonomy value, using a visually distinct color per distinct taxonomy cluster

vision.paraphrase: Nodes must be colored by folder taxonomy to visually group and distinguish content clusters.
Node color-coding by folder/taxonomy cluster mirrors content structure and organizes the graph visually.

conops.paraphrase: The force-directed graph renders nodes colored by folder/taxonomy cluster for visual organization.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall render a small distinct status dot per node reflecting its status value (active, revisiting, or dormant), styled separately from the node's taxonomy color

vision.paraphrase: Status dot on each node displays active/revisiting/dormant state and must be visible and filterable.
Status dot is a small distinct indicator styled separately from taxonomy color to show engagement/freshness.

conops.paraphrase: Each node displays a status dot indicating its active/revisiting/dormant state.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall display a title tooltip when a visitor hovers over a node

conops.paraphrase: Visitors can hover over nodes to see title tooltips, enabling quick preview of node content.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall center and zoom the view on a clicked node with an animated transition lasting approximately 900 milliseconds

vision.paraphrase: Click-to-node animation smoothly centers and zooms on clicked nodes with ~900ms duration for snappy interaction.
Click interactions feel snappy with ~900ms center/zoom animation, not instant jump-cut or sluggish delay.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor clicks a node, the graph animates to center and zoom on that node over ~900ms.
Clicking a node triggers a ~900ms center/zoom animation.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall render correctly with an empty graph (zero nodes) without a visible error, displaying an empty-state message instead

vision.paraphrase: The 'generic point-at-a-repo tool' and 'live-feeling static graph' goals imply the page must degrade gracefully rather than break when a vault (e.g. a not-yet-populated public vault) yields zero nodes.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall remain interactive (pannable, zoomable, clickable) when rendering a graph of at least 40 nodes matching the seed public vault's target scale

vision.paraphrase: The seed public vault contains 40+ sourced references; the graph must remain interactive at this scale.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall fit the force-directed graph to the viewport on initial render so that every node is visible without the visitor panning or zooming

vision.paraphrase: Initial camera framing is a critical first impression; nodes must be legible and visible without requiring immediate navigation, addressing the issue #4 finding A2.

conops.paraphrase: When the force-directed graph renders on initial load, the camera fits all nodes within the viewport so the visitor sees the full graph without panning.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall render the force-directed graph at a zoom level where node labels are legible on initial load

vision.paraphrase: Legible labels on initial load reduce the friction for first-time visitors to start reading node content without extra zooming.

conops.paraphrase: When the graph renders at the initial zoom level, node labels remain legible without the visitor zooming in further.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall provide a visible reset-view control that re-fits the force-directed camera so every node is visible when activated

vision.paraphrase: A reset-view control allows visitors to restore the initial framing after exploring via pan/zoom, providing an easy return to the overview.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor activates the reset-view control, the force-directed camera re-fits to show all nodes in the viewport.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall land a clicked node at the visual center of the graph canvas when its click-to-zoom animation completes

vision.paraphrase: Centering the clicked node fixes the issue #4 finding A6, where nodes landed off-center, breaking the visual affordance of 'clicking zooms to that node'.

conops.paraphrase: After the click-to-center-zoom animation completes, the selected node rests at the canvas center, not off-edge.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall render a selection ring or halo around the currently selected node, distinguishing it from every unselected node

vision.paraphrase: A visible selection indicator provides clear visual feedback for the active node, fixing issue #4 finding A6 where selection was ambiguous.

conops.paraphrase: When a node is selected, a ring or halo renders around it to visually distinguish the active selection.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall highlight a selected node's directly connected nodes and edges while dimming nodes unrelated to the selection

vision.paraphrase: Connection highlighting and dimming clarifies which nodes relate to the selected node, addressing issue #4 finding A6 to make the graph more readable on click.

conops.paraphrase: When a node is selected, connected nodes and edges highlight while unrelated nodes dim, showing the selection's neighborhood.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall render force-directed edge and link colors that remain visible against the active theme's canvas background in both dark and light themes

vision.paraphrase: Theme-aware edge colors ensure the graph remains readable in both dark and light themes, addressing issue #4 finding A6.

conops.paraphrase: When the visitor switches themes, edge colors adapt to remain visible against the new canvas background.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall hide force-directed node labels below a zoom threshold so that a zoomed-out view renders as readable nodes rather than overlapping text

vision.paraphrase: Label decluttering at zoom-out levels fixes issue #4 finding A6, preventing an unreadable wall of overlapping text when the visitor zooms out to see the full graph.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor zooms out on the force-directed graph, node labels disappear to keep the display readable, reappearing as they zoom in.
